readings: Take the laboratory test records that match a patient by patient ID (tests with no matching patient are left out) and group them by the patient's `SEX`, treating an empty-string sex value as a group of its own. For each sex group whose number of test records is above the average number of records per group, show the sex, its number of test records, that number as a fraction of the total over all these groups, and how far its count is above the per-group average, all unrounded.
queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM Laboratory l
  JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
  GROUP BY p.SEX
),
s AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) * 1.0 AS total FROM g
)
SELECT g.SEX, g.cnt, g.cnt / s.total AS fraction, g.cnt - s.avg_cnt AS diff_from_avg
FROM g, s
WHERE g.cnt > s.avg_cnt;
